And in a galaxy of widespread travel and shipping, there is always work for a good pilot.

A Pilot counts the following skills as career skills: {@skill Astrocartography}, {@skill Coordination}, {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Mechanics}, {@skill Operating}, {@skill Piloting}, {@skill Ranged (Light)}, and {@skill Vigilance}. Before spending experience during character creation, a Pilot may choose four of their career skills and gain one rank in each of them.
If you have a Pilot character, you may choose to start with the following gear instead of spending credits during Step 7 of character creation:
gear: A {@gear heavy pistol} {@i or} a {@gear survival kit} and a {@gear breath mask and respirator}
An {@gear Adrenaline Shot (1 dose)|adrenaline shot} and a {@gear stun baton} {@i or} a {@gear light pistol}
{@gear Durable clothing} and a {@gear carry bag}

description: Here are a few suggestions for talents that may be especially appropriate for "typical" Pilot characters.

career.name: Scoundrel
description: The Milky Way is a place of business, and surprisingly large amounts of it are, at best, of questionable legality. The Scoundrel has learned early that to survive they need to be willing to cheat, sneak, steal, and always look out for themselves first when it comes to making deals. Their palette of social abilities is widespread, and they know how to find and interact with the right kind of people.

A Scoundrel counts the following skills as career skills: {@skill Charm}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Knowledge (Underground)}, {@skill Ranged (Light)}, {@skill Skulduggery}, {@skill Stealth}, and {@skill Streetwise}. Before spending experience during character creation, a Scoundrel may choose four of their career skills and gain one rank in each of them.
If you have a Scoundrel character, you may choose to start with the following gear instead of spending credits during Step 7 of character creation:
gear: A {@gear combat knife} {@i or} 2 {@gear brass knuckles}
An {@optionFeature outlaw} {@gear submachine gun} and 2 {@gear riotfoam grenade|riotfoam grenades}
2 {@gear medi-gel} and 2 doses of {@gear Videlicit (1 dose)|Videlicit}

description: Here are a few suggestions for talents that may be especially appropriate for "typical" Scoundrel characters.

career.name: Socialite
description: Whether a child of a rich house, a diplomat, merchant or merely a good-natured bartender who gets along with everyone, the Socialite is at ease in any social interaction. They are able to charm, motivate and lead people just as easily as they can spin them tales or haggle them about the price of wares, and when they do, it's most often to their own benefit or that of their party and people.

A Socialite counts the following skills as career skills: {@skill Charm}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Knowledge (Society)}, {@skill Leadership}, {@skill Melee}, {@skill Negotiation}, and {@skill Streetwise}. Before spending experience during character creation, a Socialite may choose four of their career skills and gain one rank in each of them.
If you have a Socialite character, you may choose to start with the following gear instead of spending credits during Step 7 of character creation:
gear: {@gear Diplomat's attire} and a {@gear cultural etiquette manual} {@i or} {@gear durable clothing} and a {@gear mercantile datapad}
A {@gear combat knife} {@i or} a {@gear stun baton}
2 doses of {@gear Videlicit (1 dose)|Videlicit} {@i or} 2 doses of {@gear Creeper (1 dose)|Creeper}
A {@gear datapad} and an {@gear encrypted personal radio}

description: Here are a few suggestions for talents that may be especially appropriate for "typical" Socialite characters.

career.name: Soldier
description: Soldiers are warriors through and through. Whether they are private militia, mercenaries for hire, or enlisted in the military of their species, they are at home on the battlefield. They strike hard, fast and precise, making use of their tactical expertise, their training in various combat techniques, and always keeping their attention and iron will under pressure.

A Soldier counts the following skills as career skills: {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Brawl}, {@skill Coercion}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Knowledge (Warfare)}, {@skill Ranged (Heavy)}, and {@skill Vigilance}. Before spending experience during character creation, a Soldier may choose four of their career skills and gain one rank in each of them.
If you have a Soldier character, you may choose to start with the following gear instead of spending credits during Step 7 of character creation:
gear: {@gear Light armor} and a {@gear heavy pistol} {@i or} an {@optionFeature outlaw} {@gear assault rifle} and 2 {@gear brass knuckles} and a {@gear flashbang grenade}
{@gear Cargo Apparel|Cargo clothing} {@i or} {@gear load bearing gear}
2 {@gear medi-gel} {@i or} 1 {@gear numbcaine} {@i or} 1 {@gear Adrenaline Shot (1 dose)|adrenaline shot}

description: Here are a few suggestions for talents that may be especially appropriate for "typical" Soldier characters.

career.name: Tradesperson
description: A catchall term for anyone trained in a variety of jobs that focus on manual labor. From mechanics, over dockworkers, to asteroid miners, a Tradesperson is trained well in the skills that make up their job profile and a professional in their field, and is usually approachable and chatty about business or the latest rumors among the common people.

A Tradesperson counts the following skills as career skills: {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Driving}, {@skill Mechanics}, {@skill Melee}, {@skill Negotiation}, {@skill Operating}, {@skill Resilience}, and {@skill Streetwise}. Before spending experience during character creation, a Tradesperson may choose four of their career skills and gain one rank in each of them.
If you have a Tradesperson character, you may choose to start with the following gear instead of spending credits during Step 7 of character creation:
gear: A {@gear large hammer} {@i or} a {@gear mercantile datapad} and a {@gear portable toolkit}
A {@gear portable toolkit} {@i or} 2 {@gear gel repair patch|gel repair patches} and a {@gear baton}
2 {@gear medi-gel} and a {@gear breath mask and respirator}
{@gear Cargo Apparel|Cargo clothing} {@i or} {@gear durable clothing} and a {@gear carry bag}

description: Here are a few suggestions for talents that may be especially appropriate for "typical" Tradesperson characters.

quality.name: Phasic
description: When attacking with a weapon that possesses this quality, ignore {@dice setback} added to the check equal to the weapon's Phasic rating. This only affects {@dice setback} added by the kinetic barriers of an armor or by biotic or tech powers. When dealing damage to a synthetic target, increase the damage dealt by a number equal to the weapon's Phasic rating.

gear.name: Assault Rifle
description: While uncommon to be carried by civilians, any public or private security outfit has a sizable armory of these fully automatic weapons. Not only do they feature high fire-rates, they can also cover sizable distances on the battlefield, and only a few rounds can prove lethal.

gear.name: Heavy Pistol
description: Packing more of a punch than standard pistol models, these are found more commonly with militaries, private mercenaries or enforcers or among the civilians of colonies dealing with aggressive wildlife.

gear.name: Light Pistol
description: A small, personal firearm found with the majority of law enforcement and security personnel, but also very popular on frontier worlds and colonies or carried by civilians who may fear for their safety.
Add {@dice setback} to any checks to find a hidden light pistol on a character.

gear.name: Marksman Rifle
description: Trading the fully automatic fire capability for more precision, these rifles are often found with designated marksmen of the military (giving them their name) but have also seen plenty use as replacements for high caliber snipers with law enforcement.

gear.name: Shotgun
description: As a classic implement of home defense and hunting implement, shotguns still see high popularity among mercenary outfits. Krogan mercenaries are almost infamous for carrying these and using them to devastating effect up close.

gear.name: Sniper Rifle
description: High caliber weaponry, generally only employed by military outfits. These weapons have large stopping power and tremendous accuracy over range, but tend to fill their thermal clip after only a few shots.
After this weapon has run out of its limited ammo, it may be reloaded with the {@gear spare thermal clip} item (see page 62).

gear.name: Submachine Gun
description: A popular outfit for a variety of private security contractors, submachine guns are light and easy to carry while offering very high offensive potential. The high fire rates can make them very lethal within confined spaces.

gear.name: Flame Thrower
description: While popular tools for plant removal, it has been widely agreed in the galaxy that the use of flame throwers against organic targets is unnecessary cruelty and heavily punished by military courts...provided the user survives that long. Nevertheless, these weapons have seen increasing popularity with {@rule mercenary groups} such as the Blood Pack due to the fearsome effects they have.

gear.name: Grenade Launcher
description: Grenade launchers fire explosive projectiles with similar power to that of a hand grenade. While they are less powerful than artillery or missile launchers, they are more portable, and their smaller payloads allow multiple shots before reloading.

The listed price for the grenade launcher does not include ammunition. The profile shown is for a grenade launcher using normal {@gear high explosive grenade|high-explosive grenades}, but they can be loaded with any other grenade found in Table 2-2: Explosives and Ordnance. A small toolkit to convert hand grenades into launcher grenades is included with the weapon. Additional grenades to reload the launcher cost 100 credits, are restricted and have an encumbrance of 1 while not loaded in the launcher.

gear.name: Light Machine Gun
description: A heavy support weapon used to provide covering fire and tear apart enemy cover positions. This weapon is rarely seen away from actual battlefields, and civilian possession is illegal.

gear.name: Light Accelerator Cannon
description: Weighing in somewhere between an anti-materiel rifle and the weaponry found on vehicles, these massive cannons drive a solid metal slug with a powerful mass accelerator. The projectile reaches high velocities and the resulting thermal and kinetic energy pierces through most armor with ease.

gear.name: Missile Launcher
description: Designed for use against vehicles, these launchers can tear through dropships and light armored transports in an instant, not to mention their effect on organic targets. As such, they are only found in military operations or very well equipped mercenary organizations.
Additional missiles to reload the launcher cost 700 credits and are encumbrance 1.

gear.name: Arc Grenade
description: A high capacity charge combined with an EMP which does devastating damage to any electronic system.

Arc grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental. When targeting vehicles or synthetics, damage dealt is dealt to them as system strain or strain respectively.

gear.name: Breaching Charge
description: Designed to breach doors, walls or windows on buildings, these shaped charges are low in power, as to not unintentionally harm anyone inside. Despite this, standing directly behind a breached surface is still going to be very harmful.

Breaching charges are not thrown like grenades, but rather set with an {@difficulty easy|Mechanics}, with each uncanceled {@symbols s} increasing the damage of the explosion by one. These charges are commonly set with a timer, but can also be linked with a detonator, which is triggered with a maneuver.

gear.name: Demolition Charge
description: The larger sibling of the {@gear breaching charge}, designed to destroy vehicles or buildings.

Demolition charges are not thrown like grenades, but rather set with an {@difficulty easy|Mechanics}, with each uncanceled {@symbols s} increasing the damage of the explosion by one. Multiple charges can be set together, with each of them increasing the difficulty of the check by one and increasing the resulting damage by 15 for each additional charge. These charges are commonly set with a timer, but can also be linked with a detonator, which is triggered with a maneuver. Their {@quality Blast} quality affects all targets in short range.

gear.name: Flashbang Grenade
description: Commonly used by law enforcement, these grenades disorient targets with a bright flash and deafening thunder crack.

Flashbang grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental. If a character activates a flashbang grenade's {@quality Disorient} quality, it affects all characters at short range from the target (even if they are not damaged by the weapon).

gear.name: Frag Grenade
description: An explosive charge packed with shrapnel and a violently fragmenting casing. These grenades are highly lethal to unarmored targets.
Frag grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental.

gear.name: High Explosive Grenade
description: The most commonly used grenade found on the battlefields around the galaxy, consisting of an explosive charge in a compound casing, specifically designed to not create shrapnel.
High explosive grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental.

gear.name: Homing Grenade
description: While their explosion radius is limited, these grenades compensate by homing in on the target to guarantee a hit.

gear.name: Inferno Grenade
description: These devices are filled with an incendiary compound that spreads quickly and causes grievous harm to organic targets. Possession of these weapons is illegal, and their use is frowned upon even in military engagements.
Inferno grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental.

gear.name: Multi-frag Grenade
description: A packed bundle of smaller explosive charges that split up after being thrown, affording multiple hits against a target.
Multi-frag grenades only feature impact detonators and can not be set with a timer.

gear.name: Riotfoam Grenade
description: A non-lethal immobilization device in use by most law enforcement organizations in the galaxy. Riotfoam is a quickly expanding and hardening polymer that remains stable and rigid, making it hard for perpetrators to escape.

Riotfoam grenades can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental. A riotfoam grenade's {@quality Ensnare} quality triggers automatically on any target the weapon hits, with no need to spend {@symbols a}. Escaping hardened riotfoam requires a {@difficulty hard|Athletics}.

gear.name: "Trobor" Charge
description: Named after the krogan word for "ash heap" - as that is all it leaves behind - this thermobaric charge is easily twice the size of a normal grenade and quite heavy, but possesses a tremendous amount of explosive force. A leftover of the krogan's early wars among themselves, the weapon later saw extensive use against rachni, devastating their swarms, as well as in Krogan Rebellions. To this day, these weapons are still foolishly employed in clan feuds.

Trobor charges can be set to detonate on contact or set with a timer to detonate up to three rounds after being activated. Setting the timer can be done as an incidental. Their {@quality Blast} quality affects all targets in short range.

gear.name: Brass Knuckles
description: A universal staple among all brawlers, brass knuckles are light, concealable, and very dangerous in the right hands.

gear.name: Enforcement Gauntlet
description: An armor-plated gauntlet fitted with an array of overcharged kinetic barrier generators that allows it to deliver heavy blows that send opponents flying. Originally designed and used by the Batarian Hegemony for law enforcement purposes, the device has since become popular among the organized crime, pirates, slavers and gladiators in the Terminus systems.

gear.name: Venom Gauntlet
description: Infamously used by the turian Cabal units, these long, slender claws are not only vicious slashing weapons, they are also hollow on the inside in order to deliver a variety of drugs with their attacks.

A venom gauntlet can be loaded with up to 3 doses of poisons or drugs. Upon a successful combat check that inflicts one or more wounds, the target suffers the effects of being exposed to the substance, consuming one of the loaded doses.

gear.name: Baton
description: Often wielded by security and law enforcement in order to non-lethally pacify intruders and lawbreakers.

gear.name: Combat Knife
description: Commonly carried by any explorers and adventurers, as well as most soldiers and mercenaries, these knives can serve a variety of survival purposes, while also having use as a backup weapon.

gear.name: Monomolecular Sword
description: With a blade sharpened to the thinnest possible point, these blades can easily cleave through most organic material as well as some layers of armor. Unfortunately, their sharpness can lead inexperienced users to seriously injure themselves.

gear.name: Large Hammer
description: Heavy weighted bludgeons, often used in (de-)construction business, though many of them have seen use as weapons. Some models may have their crushing power augmented through use of pistons and mass effect fields.
Among krogan, heavy hammers are weapons of ceremony and war and are only found carried by senior warriors, battlemasters and warlords.
A large hammer requires two hands to wield.

gear.name: Riot Shield
description: Found in {@rule C-Sec}'s armory as well as with some frontline combatants that make use of this shield's excellent defensive properties. Recently shields like these have often been seen on {@rule Cerberus} units.

gear.name: Stun Baton
description: Often wielded by security and law enforcement in order to non-lethally pacify intruders and lawbreakers.

gear.name: Biotic Lashes
description: These unique weapons are byproducts of the {@rule Cerberus} Project Phoenix, to be carried by their heavily augmented biotic soldiers. They are difficult to wield, but deadly in the right hands.
When making a combat check with Biotic Lashes, ignore any defense the target gains from {@rule cover}.

gear.name: Adas Anti-Synthetic Rifle
description: Named in memory to those killed on the planet Adas during the Morning War, this quarian designed weapon shoots electrically charged, concussive plasma bolts at impressive ranges.
When making a combat check with an Anti-Synthetic Rifle, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} from a check with this weapon to cause it to run out of ammo.

gear.name: Arc Projector
description: Designed in a {@rule Cerberus} research lab as an effective weapon to combat geth, this device uses an ionizing laser to paint a target, then fires a high-voltage electrical strike along the path, which can spread to other targets.

This weapon has to be fired with the {@quality Auto-fire} quality, increasing the difficulty of the attack. Your GM may spend {@symbols hhh} from a check with this weapon to cause it to hit an unintended target.

gear.name: Kishock Harpoon Gun
description: This sniper rifle launches a unique, harpoon-like spike outfitted with microscopic disruptors that cause massive internal injuries to organic targets and can even tear synthetics apart. These weapons are favored by batarian pirates who care little if their targets survive the encounter.

When this weapon inflicts a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}, it results in an "At the Brink" effect, unless the roll on {@b {@table I.6-10: Critical Injury Result}} on page 115 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook would result in a more grievous injury.
Additional harpoons to reload the weapon cost 100 credits and are encumbrance 0.

gear.name: Reegar Carbine
description: A weapon designed by the quarian fleet to combat geth and other synthetic targets. They function by use of an ionizing laser, which then allows a strong current to arc towards the target.

gear.name: STG Scorpion
description: A unique pistol used by the salarian special forces which fires low-velocity, squash-head projectiles that first stick to the target with adhesive coating and then explode.

Instead of firing at a target, a Scorpion projectile can be shot at a surface. It will remain there for 3 rounds or until an opponent gets close enough, at which point it detonates and inflicts damage equal to its {@quality Blast} rating.

gear.name: Cargo Apparel
description: A mainstay of clothing style among dockworkers, freight pilots, engineers and craftsmen. Outfits like these feature various extra pockets.
A character wearing cargo clothing may carry up to three items of encumbrance 1 or lower without those items counting toward their {@rule Encumbrance Values|encumbrance value}.

gear.name: Diplomat's Attire
description: Elegant robes, fancy suits or ceremonial garb, attire like this exudes an aura of authority and officialism.
A character wearing diplomat's attire adds {@dice boost} to any checks to claim diplomatic authority, fit in with high-society or bypass normal protocol.

gear.name: Durable Clothing
description: This catch-all category describes any clothes that can take some wear and tear, from normal everyday colonists' gear to the uniforms worn upon military ships.

gear.name: Sealed Environmental Suit
description: A sealed environmental suit is a catchall for the armor needed by certain species to survive outside of their highly unusual environments. The design depends on the species involved. Quarians, while adapted to common nitrogen-oxygen environments rely on a suit which isolates them from their surroundings due to their weak immune system. Volus on the other hand must be kept in a high-pressure ammonia atmosphere, as they can not survive for long outside it.

A sealed environmental suit must be designed for a specific species (chosen when it is purchased). While wearing it, the wearer may survive in hostile environments indefinitely (at the GM's discretion, as some environments such as the crushing depths of a gas giant or the burning glare of a star are too much for any equipment to resist).

gear.name: Light Armor
description: The lightest and most basic armor, often worn by security personnel like {@rule C-Sec} or biotic specialists that can not afford to sacrifice their mobility.

gear.name: Medium Armor
description: Common armor suits worn by the majority of military ground troops and mercenary forces. Its plating affords it higher damage absorption, though at the cost of mobility.
A character wearing medium armor adds {@dice setback} to any {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Coordination} checks they make.

gear.name: Heavy Armor
description: These heavy suits of armor are rarely seen in public. They are popular among krogan, to whom an ancient, battleworn, set of heavy armor is a family heirloom, or given to elite soldiers intended to function as one-man-armies.
A character wearing heavy armor adds {@dice setback|2} to any {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Coordination} checks they make.

gear.name: Basic Omni-tool
description: All omni-tools feature the following basic features: flashlight, scanner, remote device access, basic repair tool, {@gear medi-gel} dispenser, camera, video, audio and holographic communication, video game console and a small flash-forge fabricator. More specialized tools can also offer unique abilities and strengthen the damage of tech attacks.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Bluewire Omni-tool
description: A basic, but cheap and reliable omni-tool produced by Aldrin Labs. Enthusiasts praise it for its simplistic interfaces, but critics speak of its sub-par performance in combat.
When casting any tech power, the character reduces the difficulty of the check by one.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Chameleon Omni-tool
description: Sirta Foundation refuses on principle to produce weaponry but excels at creating defensive- and support-specialized omni-tools.

When the character casts the {@spell Tech Augment|Tech Armor} or {@spell Tech Augment|Tactical Cloak} power, they may add the Additional Target and Range effects without increasing the difficulty. In addition, this tool comes with the {@gear Advanced First Aid} module permanently installed, which consumes no slot.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Cipher Omni-tool
description: Manufactured by the volus-owned Elkoss Combine Corporation in the Terminus systems, this affordable tool is optimized for system analysis and intrusion.

When the character casts the {@spell Sabotage} power, the first effect added increases the difficulty one less than it usually would. In addition, tech attacks cast by the character increase their damage by three.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Enforcer Omni-tool
description: A relatively new model developed by Elanus Risk Control Services, the Enforcer omni-tool is optimized for law enforcement and security service duties, though some claim its limiters may not work properly.

When the character casts a {@spell Tech Attack} power, they may add the Non-Lethal and Close Combat effects without increasing the difficulty. In addition, they must add the Blast effect with no increase in difficulty. Tech attacks cast by the character increase their damage by two.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Logic Arrest Omni-tool
description: A combat optimized tool by Ariake Technologies, designed to increase the effective range and power of tech specialists in the field.
When the character casts a tech power, the first Range effect added does not increase the difficulty. In addition, tech attacks increase their damage by four.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Nexus Omni-tool
description: Produced by Armali Council, this omni-tool offers passive support for tech constructs, using subroutines and passive energy management to sustain them.

When the character casts a {@spell Tech Construct} power, the construct remains summoned until the end of the encounter without the character having to use the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}. In addition, tech attacks increase their damage by two.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Polaris Omni-tool
description: Kassa Fabrication has made a name for itself in producing some of the finest armor in the galaxy. They are now slowly extending their excellent quality to the omni-tool market.
When the character casts a {@spell Tech Attack} power, they may add the Blast effect without increasing the difficulty. In addition, tech attacks cast by the character increase their damage by three.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Savant Omni-tool
description: One of the top of the line models on the market, the Savant series by Serrice Council excels in the tasks it has been programmed for, but good equipment has its price.

When the character readies a tech power, they may choose any one effect that increases the difficulty of that power by one. The effect does not increase the difficulty. This bonus can only affect one effect on one power at the same time. In addition, tech attacks cast by the character increase their damage by three.
{@b Slots:} This omni-tool's hard points are slots, which can only be filled with omni-tool software and omni-blades.

gear.name: Advanced First Aid
description: A favorite among emergency responders and battlefield medics, this collection of upgrades provides a quick access to {@gear medi-gel} as well as improved scanners to assess patient conditions.

When the character makes a {@skill Medicine} or {@skill Knowledge (LifeSci)} check, they add {@symbols a} to the results. Once per encounter, the character may draw and use a {@gear medi-gel} as an incidental.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Advanced Scanner
description: A common sight among {@rule C-Sec} officers, mechanics and merchants alike, this upgraded scanning software for the omni-tool can help diagnose mechanical and electrical failure in devices, as well as find irregularities in material, or highlight objects that may have gone amiss otherwise.

When using the scanner, add {@symbols a} to the results of all {@skill Perception} checks to investigate an environment and to all {@skill Mechanics} or {@skill Computers} checks to diagnose failure on a device.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Combat Sensors
description: Often colloquially referred to as "radar" or "motion sensor", this VI-assisted sensor suite monitors the position of allies while also using algorithms to calculate strategically possible enemy positions.
When making a {@skill Cool} or {@skill Vigilance} check to {@rule determine Initiative|determine initiative}, add {@dice boost|2} to the dice pool.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Encrypted Comms
description: By use of multiple, layered encryption protocols, this software guarantees high security on all voice, video and holographic communication.
Any attempt to intercept and decrypt messages sent from this omni-tool requires a {@difficulty formidable|Computers}.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Supercharged Components
description: Experimental software that exceeds the safety limits on parts of the omni-tool hardware to boost the output of tech powers.

As an incidental when the character casts a {@spell Tech Attack} power, they may upgrade the difficulty of the check once to add the {@quality Pierce} quality with a rating equal to their ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)} to the check.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: VI Ability Support
description: A powerful, but not fully developed tech power assistance software. The VI tends to not always recognize when its assistance is required, though future firmware updates might fix that.
When the character generates {@symbols t} while casting a tech power, you may roll {@dice boost} and add it to the results in addition to spending the {@symbols t} normally.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Common Omni-Blade
description: Flash-forged close-combat weaponry is almost as old as omni-tools themselves. Many soldiers value the ability to deploy a melee weapon in an instant without having to worry about extra weight or storage problems.

As a maneuver, if the character has a free hand, they may draw their omni-blade, which appears attached to their arm as an extension of their omni-tool. The weapon can be dismissed again as an incidental.

The model of omni-blade determines the combat skill used, their price and rarity. All omni-blades have encumbrance 0 when deployed and they do not count against having a free hand for the purposes of casting tech powers. Note that despite the name, not all omni-blades are close-combat weaponry.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

{@b Special Rules:} The Twin Omni-blades require both hands to use.
{@b Slots:} This item's hard points are the omni-tool slots it fills; it can only be installed in an omni-tool.

gear.name: Actuar Biotic Amp
description: Designed by Binary Helix as a work-assisting amplifier, this device is specifically tuned to improve a user's telekinetic abilities.
When the character casts the {@spell Telekinesis} power, they reduce its difficulty by one.

gear.name: Gemini Biotic Amp
description: A public release of a turian military amp produced by Armax Arsenal. Originally designed to be used by Cabal units, it's optimized for quick, precise and close up strikes. For the civil release, the damage amplification was reduced.
When the character casts the {@spell Attack} power, they may add the Charge and Close Combat effects without increasing the difficulty. Biotic attacks increase their damage by two.

gear.name: Polaris Biotic Amp
description: With Kassa Fabrication being new to the market of biotic amps, they have chosen to target niches to improve their public appeal. These amplifiers assist the user in keeping their focus, though users have reported occasional headaches as a side-effect.

Once per round, while using this biotic amp, a character may suffer one strain to perform a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver} to sustain a biotic power as an incidental. In addition, biotic attacks increase their damage by three.

gear.name: Prodigy Biotic Amp
description: Armali Council is well renowned for producing high quality biotic amps sold only to a select few, wealthy clients. These amps are tuned specifically to the client's wishes.

When the character acquires this biotic amp, they may choose up to two effects with a total added difficulty of three or less. They may add these effects to any appropriate ability without increasing its difficulty.

gear.name: Savant Biotic Amp
description: Known as the most powerful biotic amp on the market, the Savant series by Serrice Council are rare and only sold to customers after a thorough background check.
When the character casts a biotic power, the first Range effect added does not increase the difficulty. In addition, biotic attacks increase their damage by four.

gear.name: Solaris Biotic Amp
description: Simple, affordable and reliable are three core features praised about Aldrin Labs products. Their biotic amps are no exception, providing good statistics across the board and universally applicable features.

When the character casts the {@spell Augment} power, the first effect added increases the difficulty one less than it usually would. In addition, biotic attacks cast by the character increase their damage by three.

gear.name: Unity Biotic Amp
description: Following Sirta Foundation's principle of not producing offensive technologies, their Unity model amplifier is designed to assist users in providing support to multiple allies nearby.

When the character casts a biotic power, they may add the Additional Target effect without increasing the difficulty. Additionally, the first Range effect added to the {@spell Barrier}, {@spell Augment} or {@spell Domination} power does not increase the power's difficulty.

gear.name: Armor-Piercing Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.
{@b Armor-Piercing Ammunition:} The weapon gains the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 2} quality or increases its existing {@quality Pierce} quality by 1.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Cryo Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.
{@b Cryo Ammunition:} The weapon gains the {@quality Ensnare|Ensnare 2} quality or increases its existing {@quality Ensnare} quality by 2.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Disruptor Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.
{@b Disruptor Ammunition:} The weapon gains the {@quality Phasic|Phasic 2} quality or increases its existing {@quality Phasic} quality by 2.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Explosive Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.

{@b Explosive Ammunition:} The weapon gains the {@quality Disorient|Disorient 2} quality or increases its existing {@quality Disorient} quality by 1. A character may spend {@symbols t} from a combat check made with the weapon to {@rule staggered|stagger} the target for one round.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Incendiary Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Shredder Ammunition
description: Ammunition upgrades can modify the properties of projectiles, adjusting the effectiveness of weapons in various combat situations.
{@b Shredder Ammunition:} The weapon gains the {@quality Vicious|Vicious 3} quality or increases its existing {@quality Vicious} quality by 2.

A character may spend a maneuver, consuming the ammunition upgrade, to apply it to their weapon or the weapon of a character they are engaged with. The weapon retains the benefits until it runs out of ammo, however, the GM may spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} to cause an upgraded weapon to run out of ammunition.

gear.name: Smoke Grenade
description: Smoke grenades contain a chemical compound which, when ignited, burns into a thick, blinding smoke. The compound comes in a variety of colors, making the devices useful to mark areas as well as provide {@rule cover}.

As a maneuver, a character can throw a smoke grenade at a point within short range. The grenade quickly releases a thick cloud of smoke, large enough to conceal a single character and any characters engaged with them. The smoke screen provides concealment worth +3 dice (see the {@rule Concealment (Darkness, Smoke, and Intervening Terrain)|Concealment} section on page 110 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook).

gear.name: Spare Thermal Clip
description: Thermal clips are designed to absorb the excess thermal energy generated by weapons, and after their heatsinks are at capacity, they are ejected and replaced with a fresh clip.

If a character has a spare thermal clip, they may spend a maneuver to reload and continue to use their weapon if it runs out of ammo. This consumes the extra clip. You can not reload weapons with the {@quality Limited Ammo} quality, with the exception of those that specifically say so in their descriptions.

gear.name: Carry Bag
description: Duffle bags, messenger bags and various other carryalls fall into this category. They offer a good amount of storage while being easy to carry and looking perfectly ordinary.
While wearing a carry bag, a character increases their {@rule encumbrance threshold} by 3.

gear.name: Load Bearing Gear
description: Used by most military outfits around the galaxy, this combination of vests, straps, clips and magnetic holders allows carrying various pieces of gear in easily accessible positions.
While wearing load-bearing gear, a character increases their {@rule encumbrance threshold} by 3.

gear.name: Strongbox
description: Built from strong, reinforced alloys, strongboxes (or safes or similar storages) are a common way to store and secure belongings.

A strongbox can hold a number of items with {@rule encumbrance values} totaling up to 10. They are near impervious to outside damage and anything powerful enough to break them open probably destroys the contents in the process. Their electronic, biometric locks are highly sophisticated and should prove a challenge even for an exceptionally skilled intruder.

gear.name: Comm Buoy
description: Real-time communication across the galaxy is possible thanks to networks of expensive mass relay comm buoys that can daisy-chain a transmission via lasers. They are built in patterns outward from each mass relay and work akin to relays themselves, creating small corridors of low-mass space which allows for FTL tightbeam laser communication. These buoy networks are found in all traveled areas of the galaxy, with only deep space routes and uninhabited areas resulting in ships losing comm access.

Theoretically, comm buoys can be set to separate frequencies to create networks separate from the extranet, but their price only makes this viable for large corporations, criminal enterprises and (private) militaries.

gear.name: Encrypted Personal Radio
description: These radios are small, secure devices used for personal communication. They have a limited range but are unaffected by buildings and other obstacles. They are cheap and readily available and are nearly untraceable (as they only operate with a specified network of other radios).

gear.name: Field Radio
description: Heavy-duty, military-grade transceivers carried by soldiers, field radios allow sending and receiving information on the battlefield. Traditionally assigned to, and carried by, dedicated radio operators, the devices are compact enough to be carried by one person, but powerful enough to transmit up into low orbit.

gear.name: Concussion Fist
description: A replacement piece for a user's forearm and hand, this cybernetic features a small mass effect field generator which can greatly increase the kinetic energy of its user's physical attack. Unlike most replacement limbs, this cybernetic is traditionally not covered by regenerated skin, both to assist in heat-dispersion after its use and due to the menacing effect its appearance has.

The concussion fist counts as a {@skill Brawl} weapon with the following profile ({@skill Brawl}; Damage 8; Critical 3; Range [Engaged]; {@quality Concussive|Concussive 1}, {@quality Slow-Firing|Slow-Firing 2}). The character also decreases their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Cybernetic Arm or Leg
description: Having evolved far beyond normal prosthetic replacements, cybernetic arms and legs can replace a missing limb in all its natural abilities, and can even enhance a user's physical abilities far beyond the norm. Often used in combination with cloned tissue or synthetic skin to make them appear like natural extremities, some users prefer to keep them uncovered, instead displaying their enhancements proudly.

A cybernetic arm or leg increases a character's {@characteristic Brawn} or {@characteristic Agility} rating - chosen when they obtain the limb - by 1. If a character has one or more cybernetic arms, they decrease their strain threshold by 1, and if they have one or more cybernetic legs, they decrease their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Cybereyes
description: A fairly common cybernetic, cybereyes replace a user's normal eyes (or eye), granting them greatly improved eyesight, some even providing access to the infrared or ultraviolet spectrum. This implant is popular with drell, who use it to understand the hanar's language of bio-luminescence without a translator.

One or more cybereyes increase a character's ranks in {@skill Perception} by 1 and remove {@dice setback} caused by smoke or darkness on any checks they make. A character can also display information from their omni-tool into their view. Further, they decrease their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Cyberorgan
description: Following the medicinal breakthrough of creating complete artificial organs to replace damaged or failing ones, the technology gave rise to performance-enhancing variants, which are by now a complex but reasonably common implant.
When acquiring a cyberorgan, a character may choose from the following options:

items: {@b Cybernetic Heart:} A cybernetic heart increases a character's wound threshold by 2. (This is a special exception to the attribute increase limit for cybernetics, and a character cannot increase their wound threshold by more than 2 with cybernetics.)

{@b Cybernetic Lungs:} Cybernetic lungs increase a character's ranks in {@skill Athletics} by 1 and allow them to survive up to five minutes in an unbreathable atmosphere (but not {@rule vacuum}) without {@rule suffocation|suffocating}.
{@b Cybernetic Liver:} A cybernetic liver increases a character's ranks in {@skill Resilience} by 1 and makes them immune to the effects of alcohol.

description: For each cyberorgan a character has, they decrease their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Emotional Response Analyzer
description: A small implant that combines a fast analysis unit with a database of common facial expressions and body movements for a wide array of species. A user of this cybernetic is provided with a parallel analysis of a person they engage in conversation with, which can help to detect lies or ascertain the other's emotional state.

A character with this implant adds {@dice boost|2} to checks to discern whether another character is lying as well as to checks made to ascertain another character's mental and emotional state but also decreases their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Graybox
description: Grayboxes are neural implants that serve to store a person's memories and sensations. Originally designed to treat patients suffering from Alzheimer's disease, the technology turned out to have dangerous side effects, where removal of the device or software malfunctions could cause permanent and serious brain damage. As such, grayboxes are now only given to people in need of their eidetic memory, such as researchers and intragalactic spies.

A character with a graybox possesses eidetic memory. They can perfectly recall any fact they have learned or image they have seen as an out-of-turn incidental. Should the character's controlling player not remember the specifics, the Game Master should remind them of the relevant facts. They also reduce their strain threshold by 1.

Unlike other cybernetics, installing a graybox requires a {@difficulty daunting|Medicine}. Should the implant ever be removed, the character suffers grievous brain damage, reducing their {@characteristic Intellect} by 2 (to a minimum of 1) and halving their strain threshold.

gear.name: Heavy Skin Weave
description: By weaving strong synthetic fibers through a person's skin and upper muscle layers can reduce the damage suffered from physical trauma. It's not much protection, but it is enough to turn a blade or absorb a beating.
Heavy skin weave increases a character's soak by 1 and reduces their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Microfiber Muscles
description: By perforating the muscles with micro-fibers their overall strength is increased greatly, while the potential for muscle damage from exertion is reduced. Popular with laborers and anyone relying on physical strength in their career, these improvements are considered a less invasive alternative to a full limb replacement.

A character with microfiber muscles adds {@symbols s} to the result of any {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Brawl}, or {@skill Melee} checks they make. The character also decreases their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Skeletal Lattice
description: A very invasive procedure that reinforces the skeleton with a synthetic weave making their bones almost unbreakable. While more frequently used to treat patients suffering from various degenerative bone diseases or severely broken bones, it is also popular among those laborers, colonists, soldiers, and mercenaries who can afford it.

Whenever a character with skeletal lattice suffers a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}, they may roll twice on {@table I.6-10: Critical Injury Result}, on page 115 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, and choose which of the two results to use. The character also decreases their strain threshold by 1.

gear.name: Adrenaline Shot (1 dose)
description: Mistakenly named, this "cocktail" features a combination of endorphins, epinephrine and other hormones in an autoinjector. Officially not allowed for battlefield use but still commonly found with both government militaries and mercenaries, this mix improves reaction speed and pain tolerance.

A character may use an adrenaline shot as a maneuver. Until the end of their next turn, they upgrade any {@characteristic Brawn} and {@characteristic Agility} based checks by one and may perform a second maneuver without spending strain. At the end of their next turn, they suffer 3 strain.

gear.name: Creeper (1 dose)
description: A dust-like mold grown on vines grown as nutrient food in human colonies, it enables "potent visions" or "colorful daydreams". Due to the limited production on some human colonies it is hard to find.
A character may consume a dose of Creeper as a maneuver. When they do, they heal 3 strain but are {@rule disoriented} for the remainder of the encounter (or one hour in narrative time).

gear.name: Hallex (10 doses)
description: A controlled substance, taken in pill form, which induces heightened senses and extreme euphoria in its user. It sees high popularity in the nightlife of many civilized worlds, and is said to pair well with the effects induced by melding with an asari.

Taking a dose of Hallex requires a maneuver. The character immediately recovers all strain and upgrades the difficulty of all {@characteristic Cunning} and {@characteristic Presence} related checks once for the remainder of the encounter (or one hour in narrative time). At the end of the encounter, instead of recovering from strain as described on page 117 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, the character suffers 10 strain. They may make an {@difficulty average|Resilience} to reduce the strain suffered by 1 per {@symbols s} or {@symbols aa}.

gear.name: Lethal Blood Agent (1 dose)
description: A powerful, instantaneous chemical agent that induces lethal respiration failure when ingested or inhaled.

A character affected by the toxin must make a {@difficulty formidable|Resilience}. Targets suffer 2 wounds and 2 strain per {@symbols h}, and a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury} with a +50 modifier if they fail the check. The GM may spend {@symbols d} to have the target repeat this check on their next turn.

gear.name: Minagen X3 (1 dose)
description: A highly illegal and dangerous drug, Minagen X3 can be inhaled or injected to amplify a person's biotic potential. The degree of enhancement depends on the form of exposure and dosage taken, however prolonged use of Minagen X3 can prove very dangerous to the user's health.

For transport and storage, the substance is usually moved in small, pressured, containers. As a single dose, it is most commonly sold in vials that feature a small injector needle or can be crushed to release the drug.

Each dose of Minagen X3 upgrades the ability of all {@skill Biotics} checks by one, provided the character is able to use biotic abilities. When inhaled, this effect lasts until the end of the character's next turn, when injected, the effect persists until the end of the encounter. Additionally, any character exposed to Minagen X3 must make an {@difficulty average|Resilience} for a single dose or a {@difficulty hard|Resilience} for two or more doses or suffer 2 wounds. If injected, the difficulty of this check is upgraded once.

gear.name: Minagen X3 (20 dose container)
description: A highly illegal and dangerous drug, Minagen X3 can be inhaled or injected to amplify a person's biotic potential. The degree of enhancement depends on the form of exposure and dosage taken, however prolonged use of Minagen X3 can prove very dangerous to the user's health.
