The paladin can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

gear: {@gear Logic Arrest Omni-tool}: Add +4 damage to tech attacks; the first Range effect added does not increase difficulty.
{@gear Medium Armor}: 1 defense, +2 soak; adds {@symbols s} to any {@characteristic Brawn}-based checks (with the exception of {@skill Resilience}).

adversary.name: Quarian Marksman
description: Tactical commando units of the Migrant Fleet, these soldiers undertake essential missions within geth space, sabotaging strategic positions of the enemy, salvaging tech from before the Morning War and gathering intelligence on geth movements. With their expertise at long range combat and tactical support, many foes never see them coming.
{@b Tech:} A quarian marksman can have up to 2 tech abilities readied and may select any of their additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Energy Drain
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short or medium range; if successful, until the end of the marksman's next turn, the target decreases their melee and ranged defense by up to 1 and the marksman increases their defense by an equal amount. The marksman can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Tactical Scan
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short or medium range; if successful, until the end of the marksman's next turn, reduce the Critical rating of all combat checks directed at the target by 1 (to a minimum of 1). The marksman can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Supply Pylon
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, summon a supply pylon at engaged range that lasts until the end of the marksman's next turn. While engaged with the pylon, may reload a weapon that has run out of ammunition as an incidental. The marksman can maintain this construct with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

weapons.name: Adas anti-synthetic rifle with tactical visor

gear: {@gear Logic Arrest Omni-tool}: Add +4 damage to tech attacks; the first Range effect added does not increase difficulty.

adversary.name: Turian Cabal
description: These elite soldiers of the Turian Hierarchy are a rarity in the field. As some of the few turians to feature biotic potential, they are assigned to unique infantry units that perform infiltration and assassination missions.
{@b Biotics:} Turian cabal have access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Charge
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s} and the cabal moves into engaged range with the target.

spells.name: Augment
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the cabal's next turn, they increase the ability of any of their skill checks by one. The cabal can maintain these effects with a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

weapons.name: Twin venom gauntlets
weapons.details: When a target suffers wounds from this weapon, they are immediately exposed to one of the substances the cabal carries (cabal's choice)

gear: 3 Doses {@gear Neuroparalytic (1 dose)|Neuroparalytic}: Target must make an {@difficulty average|Resilience}; if they fail, they are {@rule immobilized} for 3 rounds and are unable to perform any action that requires movement. Each {@symbols h} inflicts 1 strain on the target.

3 Doses {@gear Synthetic Neurotoxin (1 dose)|Synthetic Neurotoxin}: Target must make an {@difficulty average|Resilience}; if they fail, they suffer 5 wounds. Each {@symbols h} inflicts 1 strain on the target.
{@gear Polaris Biotic Amp}: Add +3 damage to biotic attacks; once per round may suffer one strain to perform a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver} to sustain a biotic power as an incidental.

adversary.name: Turian Havoc Soldier
description: Members of the lethal 26th Armiger Legion of the Turian Hierarchy, Havoc troopers are fast-deploying frontline assault fighters. Using the {@gear jump jets} on their armor, they propel themselves forward to launch lightning-fast strikes against unsuspecting, high-value targets.
gear: Havoc Armor: 1 defense, +2 soak; twice per encounter may use an out-of-turn incidental to fly until the end of their next turn; may damage armor by 1 step to extend this effect by one round.

{@gear Adrenaline Shot (1 dose)|Adrenaline Shot}: May be used with a maneuver; until the end of the soldier's next turn, they upgrade any {@characteristic Brawn} and {@characteristic Agility} based checks by one and may perform a second maneuver without spending strain; at the end of their next turn, they suffer 3 strain.

adversary.name: Automated Heavy Turret
description: Heavy turrets are employed as part of fortification and are found on military compounds, space stations or protecting frontier world colonies from outside threats. Their weaponry is powerful enough to even damage vehicles, making them absolutely lethal to humanoid targets.

adversary.name: Automated Light Turret
description: Light turrets are often carried into the field by engineers or fortification specialists. Once deployed, they use their automated IFF systems to target the nearest opponent and open fire with their powerful weapon systems.
Light turrets can be carried and have an encumbrance of 6 when collapsed. Deploying or undeploying them requires an action.

adversary.name: Combat Drone
description: Drones are a common and helpful tech construct. While some of them may serve more benign purposes, engineers prefer sending out combat drones on the battlefield. They are small and cheap to deploy with an omni-tool and provide at worst a distraction, at best an extra combatant.

adversary.name: Geth Colossus
description: The largest ground-combat platform in the geth arsenal, Colossi possess effective anti-infantry as well as anti-armor capabilities and can lay waste to squads of organic targets.

adversary.name: Geth Hopper
description: Designed as ambush units and outfitted with both a sniper weapon and tech-based combat functions, these platforms are unknown even to the quarians, marking them as a recent addition to the geth forces.
{@b Tech:} Geth hoppers have access to the Sabotage action and may select any of its additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Overheat
spells.description: Choose one target carrying a powered weapon in short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the weapon immediately runs out of ammo.

spells.name: Tactical Scan
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short or medium range; if successful, until the end of the hopper's next turn, reduce the Critical rating of all combat checks directed at the target by 1 (to a minimum of 1). The hopper can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

gear: Integrated Omni-tool: The first Range effect added to tech powers does not increase their difficulty.

adversary.name: Geth Hunter
description: {@skill Stealth} and infiltration units of the geth, carrying powerful plasma shotguns and outfitted with tactical cloaking devices and strong kinetic barriers.
{@b Tech:} Geth hunters have access to the Augment action but may only use the following tech power:

spells.name: Tactical Cloak
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the hunter is rendered invisible, disengages from all foes, is unable to be engaged and gains {@rule Concealment (Darkness, Smoke, and Intervening Terrain)|concealment} worth three dice.

adversary.name: Geth Pyro
description: In an unusual design choice, the geth outfitted this platform with a flamethrower, a weapon commonly known to strike fear in organic beings due to the grievous injuries it causes. While they see only rare deployment, these units are highly lethal in close combat.
gear: Tank Backpack: Flame thrower can not run out of ammo; if struck by an aimed attack that does damage exceeding soak, the tank explodes, causing 10 damage to the pyro and all engaged characters.

adversary.name: Geth Prime
description: Easily identified by their hulking size and back-mounted communications suite, the prime platforms function as field commanders to geth squads. Wielding heavy weaponry and equipped with cyber-warfare systems that provide them the support of combat drones, they are a lethal combatant on the battlefield.
{@b Tech:} Geth primes have access to the Tech Construct action but may only use the following tech power:

spells.name: Combat Drone
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, summon a {@adversary combat drone} at engaged range; the drone takes its turn immediately after the prime and attacks the nearest opponent, unless directed otherwise with a maneuver.

weapons.name: Pulse cannon
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the phasic machine gun.}

gear: Integrated Omni-tool: Tech constructs summoned by the geth prime do not require a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

adversary.name: Geth Trooper
description: The default infantry units of the geth, deployed in small groups and outfitted with only basic equipment, serving as expendable, but effective soldiers.

adversary.name: Hahne-Kedar FENRIS
description: Hahne-Kedar's "attack dog" mechs, designed to guard facilities and incapacitate intruders with their built-in tasers. While commonly deployed on {@rule Systems Alliance|Alliance} off-world colonies, they have found their way into the arsenal of various private security providers.

adversary.name: Hahne-Kedar LOKI
description: Bipedal humanoid robots created by Hahne-Kedar to serve for guard duty and security duties. Commonly deployed on {@rule Systems Alliance|Alliance} colonies, these units became exceedingly popular with certain {@rule mercenary groups}, such as Eclipse and Blue Suns, who use them as expendable robotic soldiers.

weapons.name: Submachine gun
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the light pistol.}

adversary.name: Hahne-Kedar YMIR
description: This heavy weapons platform is designed as an anti-infantry killing machine. Protected by strong armor and kinetic barriers and equipped with weaponry strong enough to damage light vehicles, these units are dangerous in the wrong hands - such as the Eclipse and Blue Suns, who frequently deploy them as heavy support units.

adversary.name: Infiltration Unit
description: First revealed to be employed by {@rule Cerberus} at the beginning of the Reaper War, these humanoid mechs are designed to perfectly mimic an organic. They accomplish this due to their advanced artificial intelligence (disregarding the Council's ban on AIs) and a synthetic flesh layer that covers their outer shell.

Although the only known unit was the unit designated "Eva Coré", a gynoid model posing to be a human researcher, it remains unknown how many of these units {@rule Cerberus} deployed. Following the discovery of Coré, the {@rule Systems Alliance|Alliance} produced their own limited number of units to serve as tactical ground forces in the war.
{@b Tech:} Infiltration units can have up to 3 tech abilities readied and may select any of their additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Twin Incineration
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make a {@difficulty daunting|Tech}; if successful, the target suffers 6 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Auto-fire} and {@quality Burn|Burn 2} qualities.

spells.name: Overload
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the target suffers 6 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Phasic|Phasic 1} quality.

spells.name: Tactical Cloak
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, until the end of the infiltration unit's next turn, it is rendered invisible, disengages from all foes, is unable to be engaged and gains {@rule Concealment (Darkness, Smoke, and Intervening Terrain)|concealment} worth three dice. The unit can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Decoy
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, summon a decoy at engaged range that lasts until the end of the unit's next turn. While engaged with the decoy, upgrade the difficulty of all combat checks targeting the unit once. The unit can maintain the decoy with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

gear: Integrated Omni-tool: Add +3 damage to tech attacks; the first Range effect added does not increase difficulty; when the character rolls {@symbols t} while casting a tech power, they roll {@dice proficiency} and add it to the results; when the character rolls {@symbols d} while casting a tech power, they roll {@dice challenge} and add it to the results.

adversary.name: CAT6 Heavy
description: Equipped with tough armor and possessing physical strength uncommon in humans, these Mercenary troops usually command squads of CAT6 troops. Their omni-shields grant them protection and their light machineguns tear targets to shreds.
{@i * This adversary's defense attribute includes the bonuses from their weapons.}

adversary.name: Eclipse Commando
description: The most lethal biotic warriors in the Eclipse. Commandos often harbor a grudge against the asari government that rejected them for service, choosing to join Eclipse to instead satisfy their hunger for power.
{@b Biotics:} Eclipse commandos have access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Warp
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 8 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 2} and {@quality Sunder} quality.

spells.name: Annihilation
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; If successful, the target suffers 8 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Burn|Burn 2} quality.

spells.name: Backlash Barrier
spells.description: Make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the commando's next turn, reduce the damage of all hits against them by one, plus one for every {@symbols ss}. The commando can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver} and spend {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} from a combat check targeting them to cause the attacker to suffer one hit causing the same total damage.

gear: {@gear Savant Biotic Amp}: Add +4 damage to biotic attacks; the first Range effect added does not increase difficulty.

adversary.name: Eclipse Vanguard
description: These troops are the strongest front-line fighters of the Eclipse mercenary company. Using their biotic abilities to devastating effects, they are able to quickly cover the gap to their opponents and deliver lethal blows.
{@b Biotics:} Eclipse vanguards have access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Charge
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s} and the vanguard moves into engaged range with the target.

spells.name: Shockwave
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Disorient|Disorient 1} and {@quality Knockdown} qualities.

gear: {@gear Gemini Biotic Amp}: Add +2 damage to biotic attacks; adding the Charge or Close Combat effects does not increase difficulty.

adversary.name: Krogan Mercenary
description: Strong built, aggressive and willing to charge head first into battle to emerge the bloodied victor, krogan are a species of true warriors. As such, many search their luck as mercenaries, some freelance, but many having joined the Blood Pack.

abilities.name: Takedown
abilities.description: As an action make an opposed {@skill Brawl} vs {@skill Resilience} check targeting an engaged opponent; if successful, target is knocked {@rule prone} and {@rule immobilized} until the end of this character's next turn.

gear: {@gear Medium Armor|Krogan Medium Armor}: 1 defense, +2 soak.

adversary.name: Mercenary Engineer
description: {@skill Tech} specialists in their mercenary company, outfitted with some of the best omni-tools they can afford. They also serve as maintenance for most of the company's equipment and vehicles.
{@b Tech:} Mercenary engineers can have up to 2 tech abilities readied and may select any of their additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Overheat
spells.description: Choose one target carrying a powered weapon in short range and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the weapon immediately runs out of ammo.

spells.name: Incinerate
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short range; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Burn|Burn 2} quality.

spells.name: Overload
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short range; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Phasic|Phasic 1} quality.

spells.name: Combat Drone
spells.description: Make a {@difficulty hard|Tech}; if successful, summon a {@adversary combat drone} at engaged range; the drone takes its turn immediately after the engineer and attacks the nearest opponent, unless directed otherwise with a maneuver; spend a maneuver to detonate the drone causing 5 damage to all engaged characters.

spells.name: Tech Armor
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, until the end of the engineer's next turn, reduce the damage of all hits against them by one, plus one for every {@symbols ss}. The engineer can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

weapons.name: Heavy pistol
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the submachine gun.}

gear: {@gear Nexus Omni-tool}: Add +2 damage to tech attacks; tech constructs remain summoned until the end of the encounter without the use of the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}; when the character rolls {@symbols t} while casting a tech power, they roll {@dice boost} and add it to the results.

adversary.name: Mercenary Heavy
description: Carrying the heaviest weapons in their company's arsenal, these soldiers are only deployed in engagements against dangerous opponents or anti-vehicular missions.

abilities.name: Big Guns
abilities.description: This character has an {@rule encumbrance threshold} of 13 and reduces the {@quality Cumbersome} rating of any weapon they carry by 1, to a minimum of 3.

weapons.name: Missile launcher
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the grenade launcher.}

weapons.name: Flame thrower
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the grenade launcher or missile launcher.}

gear: 2 spare missiles (if using the missile launcher).

adversary.name: Mercenary Sniper
description: The long range assassins and support troops within a mercenary company, outfitted with high-impact sniper weapons that make quick work of even well armored targets.

weapons.name: Sniper rifle with telescopic sight
weapons.details: Reduce the difficulty of combat checks at long or extreme range by one.

weapons.name: Burst-fire sniper rifle
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the sniper rifle with telescopic sight.}

adversary.name: Mercenary Trooper
description: This profile represents any basic soldier working within a mercenary company, be they Eclipse, Blue Suns, CAT6 or others. It can also be used to represent most common military soldiers in local, planetary armies, or other private security forces.

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the assault rifle.}

weapons.name: Submachine gun
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the assault rifle or shotgun.}

adversary.name: Veteran Engineer
description: Elite specialists found only in prominent mercenary troupes, the Veteran Engineers have long moved past tending their companies' motor pools. With their tech powers and unique {@gear omni-bow} weaponry, they have become just as much a danger on the battlefield as their fellow, more commonly equipped, soldiers.
{@b Tech:} Veteran engineers can have up to 1 tech ability readied and may select any of their additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Invasion
spells.description: Make an {@difficulty average|Tech} targeting an opponent in short or medium range; if successful, until the end of the engineer's next turn, the target decreases the ability of any skill checks using their equipment by one. The engineer can maintain these effects with the {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Overheat
spells.description: Choose one target carrying a powered weapon in short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the weapon immediately runs out of ammo.

gear: {@gear Cipher Omni-tool}: Add +3 damage to tech attacks; when using the Sabotage power, the first effect added increases the difficulty by one less than it usually would.

adversary.name: Vorcha Boom-Squad
description: Trained in the use of heavy weapons, grenades, incendiary devices and anything else dangerous and volatile, these vorcha are often used as the Blood Pack's trump card. Their weaponry is dangerous at range and not few of these pyromaniacs have been known to detonate their remaining supplies as a "parting gift" to their enemies.

weapons.name: Missile launcher
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the grenade launcher.}

weapons.name: Flame thrower
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the grenade launcher or missile launcher.}

weapons.name: 3 inferno grenades
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the 3 frag grenades.}

gear: 2 spare missiles (if using the missile launcher).

adversary.name: Vorcha Grunts
description: Employed by the Blood Pack as cannon fodder, these vicious fighters often appear in large groups, swarming their targets and overwhelming them with their sheer number, resilience and ferocity.

adversary.name: Vorcha Packleader
description: Having worked their way to the tip of the pack by being stronger, tougher and more violent than the rest of their brethren, packleaders take a lieutenant's role in the Blood Pack order.

adversary.name: Ardat-Yakshi
description: Born with a rare genetic disorder exclusive to asari purebloods, the Ardat-Yakshi possess a unique mutation of their nervous system that kills their partner when mating. Adding to that, an Ardat-Yakshi grows in mental prowess after each such encounter, and their nervous system drives them to "feed" more. Because of this, each asari discovered to suffer from the condition is given the choice: life in isolation in one of the few monasteries created for this purpose, or death. Alas, some manage to escape their fate, choosing a life on the run from the Justicars, constantly driven by their hunger for more power.
{@b Biotics:} An ardat-yakshi has access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

abilities.name: Natural
abilities.description: Once per session, may reroll any one {@skill Biotics} or {@skill Charm} check.

spells.name: Reave
spells.description: Choose one organic target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 8 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with a Critical Rating of 2 and the {@quality Vicious|Vicious 2} quality.

spells.name: Neural Devastation
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 13 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Stun Damage} quality.

spells.name: Mass Dominate
spells.description: Choose up to two non-synthetic targets at short range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the ardat-yakshi's next turn, the targets decrease the ability of any of their skill checks by one. The ardat-yakshi may spend a number of {@symbols a} to affect additional targets within range and can maintain these effects with a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Confusion
spells.description: Choose one non-synthetic target at short range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the ardat-yakshi's next turn, the target decreases the ability of any of their skill checks by one. After the target makes a check, the ardat-yakshi may change any one die in the pool not displaying a {@symbols t} or {@symbols d} to a different face. The ardat-yakshi can maintain these effects with a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Mind Control
spells.description: Choose one non-synthetic target at short range and make a {@difficulty daunting|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the ardat-yakshi's next turn, the target decreases the ability of any of their skill checks by one and must follow the ardat-yakshi's orders. The ardat-yakshi can maintain these effects with a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

gear: A bottle of {@gear hallex (10 doses)}, 1 {@gear medi-gel}.

adversary.name: Asari Archaeologist
description: During the "maiden" stage of an asari's life, they are driven to exploration; their curious mind drives them to see the galaxy and make experiences that will shape their life. This asari in particular has chosen to explore the remnants of old civilizations, such as the protheans or those that came even before them.
{@b Biotics:} Asari archaeologists have access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Levitation
spells.description: Make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, until the end of the archaeologist's next turn, they increase the ability of any of their skill checks by one and gain the ability to levitate (see page 100 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook). The archaeologist can maintain these effects with a {@rule concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.

spells.name: Biotic Orb
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 4 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Stun Damage} quality.

gear: Omni-tool with {@gear Advanced Scanner} (add {@symbols a} to any {@skill Perception} check to investigate).

adversary.name: Krogan Warlord
description: Krogan Warlords are the oldest and toughest of their kind. They rise to power within their clans by brutality, physical strength and tactical expertise that outmatches their fellow warriors. In battle, they are fearless frontline fighters, their infamous rage, tough armor and heavy weaponry all serving as good reason to start running the other direction.

abilities.name: Big Guns
abilities.description: This character has an {@rule encumbrance threshold} of 12 and reduces the {@quality Cumbersome} rating of any weapon they carry by 1, to a minimum of 3.

gear: {@gear Heavy Armor|Heavy Krogan Armor}: 2 defense, +2 soak; {@rule vacuum} sealed.

adversary.name: Krogan Battlemaster
description: With biotics being a rare ability among krogan, the few that possess them quickly rise to fame and power within their ranks. Their abilities make them powerful soldiers, earning them the unique title of "Battlemaster", and are famed to rival ten warriors of any other species. They hold no respect for honor or mercy, they will go to any lengths to achieve victory in combat, no matter how reprehensible, making them fearsome opponents on the battlefield.
{@b Biotics:} Krogan battlemasters have access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Charge
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 6 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s} and the battlemaster moves into engaged range with the target.

spells.name: Biotic Crush
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make a {@difficulty hard|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 10 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}.

spells.name: Warp Detonation
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make a {@difficulty daunting|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 10 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 2} quality.

gear: {@gear Gemini Biotic Amp}: Add +2 damage to biotic attacks; adding Charge or Close Combat effects does not increase difficulty.
{@gear Heavy Armor|Heavy Krogan Armor}: 2 defense, +2 soak; {@rule vacuum} sealed.

adversary.name: Quarian Mechanic
description: As their rite of passage, each quarian is required to undertake their Pilgrimage in which they journey out and gather some experience in life and valuable resources before returning to the Migrant Fleet. Due to their upbringing, many quarians earn some credits during this time freelancing as engineers and mechanics, and some even choose to leave the fleet for good, the experiences of their Pilgrimage encouraging them to live free.
gear: {@gear Portable toolkit}, 2 {@gear gel repair patch|gel repair patches}.

adversary.name: Yahg
description: A sapient but primitive species from the planet Parnack, Yahg are known particularly for their perceptiveness and exceedingly aggressive nature. Due to the violent fate of the Council delegation sent to Parnack, the homeworld has been declared off-limits.
With their tough skin, immense physical strength and ability to learn and adapt quickly, they are among the most dangerous species in the galaxy.

adversary.name: Collector Assassin
description: Deadly shock troopers of the collector forces, assassins carry heavy particle beams into combat, which they use to attack their foes from afar. With their high precision these weapons turn truly lethal against any unfortunate target within their sights.

adversary.name: Collector Captain
description: Leading groups of foot-soldiers into the field, these captains serve as the highest authority during deployment; that is, until a drone is possessed by Harbinger. Captains also carry within their carapace a small swarm of seeker insects, which they deploy to immobilize and harass their foes.

weapons.name: Collector assault rifle
weapons.details: This weapon has no hardpoints, but has the {@gear Outdated Heatsink} attachment built-in.

adversary.name: Collector Drone
description: Mindless soldiers of the collector forces, they march recklessly into battle to destroy anyone deemed a foe by their swarm.

weapons.name: Collector submachine gun
weapons.details: This weapon has no hardpoints, but has the {@gear Outdated Heatsink} attachment built-in.

adversary.name: Collector Guardian
description: Defensive troopers of the collector forces, the guardians deploy mobile cover positions and provide covering fire for their swarm.

weapons.name: Collector assault rifle
weapons.details: This weapon has no hardpoints, but has the {@gear Outdated Heatsink} attachment built-in.

adversary.name: Possessed Collector
description: After Harbinger, through the Collector General, assumes personal control of a collector on the field, their form changes. Their chitinous carapace cracks, energy pouring from within, and the nearly dormant biotic nodes of eezo in their nervous system activate, granting them newfound combat potential.
{@b Biotics:} A possessed collector has access to all biotic abilities except dominate and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Reave
spells.description: Choose one organic target at short range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 6 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with a Critical Rating of 2 and the {@quality Vicious|Vicious 2} quality.

spells.name: Shockwave
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 6 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Disorient|Disorient 2} and {@quality Knockdown} qualities.

spells.name: Warp Detonation
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make a {@difficulty formidable|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 9 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 2} quality.

weapons.name: Collector assault rifle
weapons.details: This weapon has no hardpoints, but has the {@gear Outdated Heatsink} attachment built-in.

adversary.name: Seeker Swarm
description: These cybernetic insects are deployed by the collectors to paralyze and incapacitate their foes, leaving them open to abduction or elimination.

adversary.name: Banshee
description: Created from a select few asari, those with the Ardat-Yakshi condition or a latent potential for it, banshee are some of the most powerful and terrifying creatures in the Reaper's arsenal. Their biotic potential empowered by their cybernetic modifications, they seek out and eliminate priority targets.
{@b Biotics:} A banshee has access to all biotic abilities and may select any of their additional effects. The biotic powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Charge
spells.description: Choose one target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target suffers 8 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s} and the banshee moves into engaged range with the target.

spells.name: Warp
spells.description: Choose one organic target at short or medium range and make an {@difficulty average|Biotics}; if successful, the target takes 8 damage + 1 damage per uncancelled {@symbols s}, with the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 2} quality.

adversary.name: Brute
description: A horrid amalgam, created from the body of a krogan, with the partial head of a turian, brutes serve as living tanks and heavy anti-infantry units of the Reaper forces. Outfitted with heavy armor-plating and powerful muscles, brutes smash through squads of soldiers and light fortifications with ease.

abilities.name: Takedown
abilities.description: As an action make an opposed {@skill Brawl} vs {@skill Resilience} check targeting an engaged opponent; if successful, target is knocked {@rule prone} and {@rule immobilized} until the end of this character's next turn.

adversary.name: Cannibal
description: Monstrous fusions of batarians and humans, these creatures make up a large part of the Reaper ground forces, due to their initial arrival in batarian space. Equipped with an arm-mounted cannon, and outfitted with the capabilities to regenerate by consuming dead husks, these creatures trigger as much terror as disgust in their foes.

adversary.name: Harvester
description: Created from creatures of the same name that usually spend their existence in the desolate landscapes of desert worlds, harvesters work as synthetic-organic air support for the Reaper ground forces. With their massive wings they cover ground quickly, and their powerful cannons decimate light infantry squads.

adversary.name: Husk
description: The first cybernetic monsters encountered by the species of the current cycle, husks were first believed to be the product of the geth, who used "dragon's teeth" in the Eden Prime War to transform humans into these creatures. Mindless slaves, completely immune to outer stimuli, the Reapers use these as expendable shock troops, assaulting enemies in swarms and tearing into them with electrically charged claws.

adversary.name: Marauder
description: Created from harvested turians, marauders are powerful fighters and support units. Still carrying their service weapons and additionally outfitted with the ability to reinforce their fellow troops' armor.

adversary.name: Ravager
description: Created from the rachni, long deemed extinct, Ravagers are mobile artillery platforms of the Reaper ground forces. They have been grafted with two powerful cannons and carry sacks of Swarmers on their body which swamp their foes.

adversary.name: Swarmer Mass
description: Created from parts organic rachni, but mostly Reaper cybernetics, these small swarms are carried into battle by Ravagers. Once released, they dash towards an enemy and attack by leaping onto them and detonating.

adversary.name: Batarian Pirate
description: Selfish, bloodthirsty and greedy, pirates are just as present in the vastness of space as they once were on the oceans of planets. They board and plunder ships, sometimes even kill or enslave the owners. Within civilized systems, pirates live at the constant threat of persecution and death by law-enforcement authorities.

weapons.name: Outlaw submachine gun
weapons.details: {@i Alternative to the outlaw shotgun.}

adversary.name: Batarian Pirate Cpt.
description: At the helm of any pirate ship stands a captain, the most cunning and ruthless of his crew. While the methods by which they board ships and deal with passengers vary, each captain is always out for the biggest score, and making sure to get away unscathed.

adversary.name: Batarian Slaver
description: The concept of slavery is not unknown in the galaxy, and "indebted working contracts" are, in fact, not uncommon in the Terminus systems and neighboring regions. Those that would kidnap and sell people however are still considered to be some of the worst scum and most horrible criminals. And yet, the business remains booming, with civilian transports not uncommonly being forced to pay tribute in the form of some of its passengers and the markets on {@rule Omega} selling slaves daily.
{@b Tech:} Batarian slavers can have up to 2 tech abilities readied and may select any of their additional effects. The tech powers they use most often are the following:

spells.name: Submission Net
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}; if successful, the target suffers 5 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}(+2 if the target is organic), with the {@quality Ensnare|Ensnare 1} and {@quality Stun Damage} qualities. May spend {@symbols t} to {@rule staggered|stagger} the target for one round.

spells.name: Incapacitation Shock
spells.description: Choose one target at short range and make a {@difficulty daunting|Tech}; if successful, the target suffers 7 damage + 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s} (+2 if the target is organic), with the {@quality Disorient|Disorient 1} and {@quality Stun Damage} qualities. May spend {@symbols t} to {@rule staggered|stagger} the target for one round.

gear: Custom Slaver Omni-tool: Add +3 damage to tech attacks; adding the Anti-Organic or Non-Lethal effects does not increase difficulty.

adversary.name: Black Marketeer
description: Black marketeers are part salesmen, part fence, all business. Having one for a contact allows turning illegal assets into legal credits, and spending those again on more questionable merchandise. These entrepreneurs take a cut for their services of course, but can acquire some rare items from all corners of the galaxy.
gear: {@gear Mercantile Datapad}: Add {@dice boost} to all {@skill Negotiation} checks to buy or sell wares in the Terminus Systems.

adversary.name: Drell Assassin
description: With assassin not being an unusual occupation for a drell working within the Compact, some of those that move away from the Primacy still choose this career to earn their living. With their strong physiology, predatory instincts and perfect memory, drell make for some of the best in the business.

weapons.name: 2 suppressed heavy pistols
weapons.details: Add {@dice setback|2} to {@skill Perception} or {@skill Vigilance} checks to locate a character firing this weapon.

adversary.name: Expert Forger
description: In a galaxy ruled (mostly) under a unified government, there is a lot of paperwork, and consequently a lot of people that simply don't have time for all that paperwork. The forger caters to these, offering their services to easily create any document, license, waiver or manifest their client needs - for the right price.

adversary.name: Information Broker
description: With the extranet allowing near-immediate transfer for information throughout the galaxy, access to this information is more important than ever before - especially access to information one is usually not privy to. Brokers run their business by buying and selling information, trading secrets and keeping a delicate balance on who knows what. Often working as parts of larger nets or cells, they dig up dirt on political figures, secret science projects and mercenary contracts.

abilities.name: Knack for It 2
abilities.description: Remove {@dice setback|2} from any {@skill Computers}, {@skill Knowledge (Underground)} and {@skill Streetwise} checks.

adversaryAbility.name: Thick Carapace
description: Remove {@dice setback} due to high temperatures from all checks and reduce any fire damage taken by 3 before applying soak.

adversaryAbility.name: Thick Fur
description: Remove {@dice setback|2} imposed by cold temperatures from all checks.

adversaryAbility.name: Tunneling
description: Can move through solid rock as if it were difficult terrain.

adversaryAbility.name: Packleader
description: Add {@dice boost} to the checks of all other allied {@adversary Varren} in the encounter.

adversaryAbility.name: Biotic Pounce
description: As an action make an opposed {@skill Biotics} vs {@skill Resilience} check targeting an opponent within short range; if successful, this character moves into engaged range and the target is knocked {@rule prone} and {@rule immobilized} until the end of this character's next turn.

adversaryAbility.name: Deploy Turret
description: As an action, may set up the carried turret, which takes its turn immediately after this character and will attack the nearest enemy; may spend a maneuver to direct the turret to shoot a different target.

adversaryAbility.name: Combat Repair
description: As an action, may make an {@difficulty average|Mechanics} targeting an engaged vehicle or synthetic character, healing one point of hull trauma or one wound per uncancelled {@symbols s}.

adversaryAbility.name: Nemesis Cybernetics
description: Reduce the {@quality Cumbersome} quality of weapons by 1; body and all carried gear disintegrates upon death.

adversaryAbility.name: Finesse
description: May use {@characteristic Agility} instead of {@characteristic Brawn} when making {@skill Melee} or {@skill Brawl} checks.

adversaryAbility.name: Good Cop / Bad Cop
description: May spend {@symbols aa} from a {@skill Charm}, {@skill Coercion}, {@skill Deception}, or {@skill Negotiation} check to upgrade the ability of an ally's social skill check targeting the same character once.

adversaryAbility.name: Escape Artist
description: After a successful combat check, may suffer 2 strain to immediately use the Tactical Cloak power as an incidental.

adversaryAbility.name: Ruthless Efficiency
description: Before making a combat check, may spend one Story Point to reduce the number of {@symbols a} needed to activate item qualities or trigger effects by one to a minimum of one.

adversaryAbility.name: Natural Biotics
description: Add +2 damage to biotic attacks; add {@symbols aa} to the result of any {@skill Biotics} skill check.

adversaryAbility.name: High-Gravity Adaption
description: May remove {@dice setback|2} imposed by high-gravity environments.

adversaryAbility.name: Ponderous
description: Can never spend more than one maneuver per turn to move.

adversaryAbility.name: Havoc Strike
description: As an action make an opposed {@skill Coordination} vs {@skill Resilience} check targeting an opponent within short range; if successful, this character moves into engaged range and the target is knocked {@rule prone} and {@rule immobilized} until the end of this character's next turn.

adversaryAbility.name: Hoverer
description: Can hover; see the {@sidebar Flying} sidebar on page 100 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook.

adversaryAbility.name: Hopper Limbs
description: Once per round, may spend a maneuver and suffer 1 strain to move to any location within short range, including vertical; can stick to walls.

adversaryAbility.name: Auto-Bracing
description: Using the {@quality Auto-fire} quality does not increase the difficulty of combat checks; each time this character triggers an additional hit, they suffer 1 strain.

adversaryAbility.name: Synthflesh Cover
description: Discerning that this character is a mech and not an organic being requires a {@difficulty formidable|Perception}.

adversaryAbility.name: Shocking Reveal
description: When this character would be {@rule incapacitated} and their true form has not been revealed to the PCs before, the GM may spend a Story Point for this character to escape the encounter. This should be accompanied by a dramatic narration of this character losing their synthflesh covering.

adversaryAbility.name: Incredible Strength
description: May wield the light machinegun with one hand, reducing its range to Medium and adding {@dice setback} to any combat checks with it.

adversaryAbility.name: Blood Rage
description: After suffering 1 wound, increase the damage of {@skill Brawl} and {@skill Melee} attacks by 1 until end of the encounter; after suffering a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}, increase the damage of {@skill Brawl} and {@skill Melee} attacks by 2 until end of the encounter.

adversaryAbility.name: Prepared Trip Mine
description: Once per encounter, as an incidental, may spend a Story Point to force an opponent within medium range to make a {@difficulty hard|Vigilance}; if they fail, they suffer 3 wounds + 1 wound per {@symbols f}; {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} may be spent to {@rule staggered|stagger} opponent for 1 round.

adversaryAbility.name: Armor-Piercing Arrow
description: May spend a maneuver to increase the {@quality Pierce} quality on the next attack with the {@gear Omni-bow} by 2; cannot be used multiple times before an attack.

adversaryAbility.name: Highly Volatile
description: May use an action to detonate their equipment, vaporizing themselves and dealing 12 damage to all engaged characters; may also use this ability immediately when they are {@rule incapacitated}.

adversaryAbility.name: Ardat-Yakshi Biotics
description: Add +3 damage to biotic attacks; reduce the difficulty of all {@skill Biotics} skill checks by one; after successfully using a biotic attack or domination power, heal 1 wound.

adversaryAbility.name: Lethal Combatant
description: Add +20 to any {@rule Critical Injuries} inflicted by this character.

adversaryAbility.name: Charge
description: When making a {@skill Brawl} or {@skill Melee} attack immediately after using a maneuver to engage a target, may spend {@symbols aaa} or {@symbols t} to use this talent to knock the target {@rule prone} and move them up to one range band away.

adversaryAbility.name: Predator's Sight
description: Remove {@dice setback|2} from any {@skill Perception}, {@skill Vigilance} or combat check due to smoke, darkness or {@rule Concealment (Darkness, Smoke, and Intervening Terrain)|concealment}.

adversaryAbility.name: Seeker Swarm
description: Once per encounter, may use an action to summon a {@adversary seeker swarm} which takes its turn immediately after this character. The swarm acts independently to attack any foes.

adversaryAbility.name: Hex Shield
description: Once per encounter, may use a maneuver to deploy a hex shield in engaged range that provides a ranged defense of 2 for up to two characters.

adversaryAbility.name: Twisted Biotics
description: Add +3 damage to biotic attacks; treat this character's ranks of {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)} and {@skill Knowledge (LifeSci)} as 2 for the purposes of adding biotic effects.

adversaryAbility.name: Hindering Mass
description: May spend a maneuver to make an opposed {@skill Coordination} versus {@skill Coordination} check targeting one engaged opponent; if successful, the opponent is {@rule immobilized}.

adversaryAbility.name: Paralyzing Sting
description: Enemies who are wounded by this character must make a {@difficulty hard|Resilience} as an out-of-turn incidental or become {@rule staggered} until the end of their next turn.

adversaryAbility.name: Synthetic Zombie
description: Does not need to breathe, eat, or drink, and can survive in {@rule vacuum} and underwater.

adversaryAbility.name: Twisted Ardat-Yakshi Biotics
description: Add +3 damage to biotic attacks; reduce the difficulty of all {@skill Biotics} skill checks by one; treat this character's ranks of {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)} and {@skill Knowledge (LifeSci)} as 2 for the purposes of adding biotic effects.

adversaryAbility.name: Petrifying Scream
description: Once per encounter, may suffer 3 strain and spend a maneuver to force all opponents in long range to make a {@difficulty hard} {@rule fear} check as an out-of-turn incidental. If they fail, they are {@rule immobilized} until the end of their next turn; {@symbols hh} from this check may be spent to {@rule disoriented|disorient} the opponent, {@symbols hhh} may be spent to {@rule staggered|stagger} them.

adversaryAbility.name: Grapple
description: As an incidental, may suffer 2 strain; all opponents must spend 2 maneuvers to disengage.

adversaryAbility.name: Impale
description: May suffer 3 strain and spend a maneuver to add the {@quality Pierce|Pierce 4} and {@quality Phasic|Phasic 2} qualities to this character's next {@skill Brawl} combat check.

adversaryAbility.name: Warp Implosion
description: When {@rule incapacitated}, this character is consumed in an implosion that destroys their body.

adversaryAbility.name: Death Lunge
description: When {@rule incapacitated}, may make one out-of-turn {@skill Brawl} attack against one engaged opponent; add {@dice boost} to this check.

adversaryAbility.name: Cannibalize
description: Once per encounter, may spend an action to consume an engaged corpse of a {@adversary husk}; this character heals 4 wounds and increases their soak by 1 for the rest of the encounter.

adversaryAbility.name: Post-Mortem Explosion
description: Explodes when {@rule incapacitated}; dealing 6 damage to all engaged characters.

adversaryAbility.name: Overwhelming Numbers
description: Add {@symbols s} to all combat checks for each minion in the group beyond the first.

adversaryAbility.name: Reinforce Ally
description: Once per encounter, may spend an action and target an engaged allied minion; the target is {@rule immobilized} and {@rule staggered} until the end of its next turn, after that it increases its soak by 1 until the end of the encounter.

adversaryAbility.name: Swarmer Sack
description: When this character suffers wounds from a combat check, may spend {@symbols hh} from the check to spawn a {@adversary Swarmer Mass} at engaged range which joins the combat encounter.

adversaryAbility.name: Acidic Blood
description: When hit by a {@skill Melee} or {@skill Brawl} attack, may spend a number of {@symbols h} to inflict the same number of wounds to the attacker.

adversaryAbility.name: Suicide Leap
description: When making a combat check, add {@symbols sss} to the result; suffer 3 wounds after the check is resolved.

adversaryAbility.name: Black Market Contacts
description: When searching the black market for items, may decrease their rarity by 2.

adversaryAbility.name: Expert Forger
description: After making a {@skill Mechanics} or {@skill Computers} check, may suffer up to 2 strain to convert that many {@symbols s} to {@symbols a}.

spell.name: Domination
structured: Biotic Domination is the use of biotics to disrupt the synaptic harmonics of an organic brain, causing the target to struggle concentrating on tasks. When using this power, a character selects one non-synthetic target in short range and makes an {@difficulty average|Biotics}. At the GM's discretion, this check can instead be an opposed {@skill Biotics} versus {@skill Discipline} check. If the check is successful, until the end of the character's next turn, the target decreases the ability of any skill check they make by one (in effect, this means they remove {@dice ability} from their checks).
Before making a domination check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-6: Domination Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the check.

additionalEffects.name: Enervate
description: If a target suffers strain for any reason, they suffer 1 additional strain.

additionalEffects.name: Range
description: Increase the range of the power by one range band. This may be added multiple times, increasing the range by one range band each time.

additionalEffects.name: Additional Target
description: The power affects one additional target within range. In addition, after using the power, you may spend {@symbols a} to affect one additional target within range (and may trigger this multiple times, spending {@symbols a} each time).

additionalEffects.name: Confusion
description: After a target makes a check, you may change any one die in the pool not displaying a {@symbols t} or {@symbols d} to a different face.

additionalEffects.name: Stasis
description: The target is {@rule staggered} and {@rule immobilized} for the duration of the spell. This effect may not be combined with the additional target effect.

additionalEffects.name: Mind Control
description: The target obeys the character's commands. The character may spend a maneuver to direct the target, allowing them to determine its action and maneuver. This effect may not be combined with the additional target effect.

spell.name: Telekinesis
structured: A common use of biotics is to lift and move objects. Many people possessing biotic abilities make use of this in their common, everyday life, but the telekinetic potential has also proven itself to be powerful on the battlefield, in creating makeshift barricades and throwing projectiles at targets. When using this power, a character selects one object of silhouette 0 that they can see within short range and makes an {@difficulty easy|Biotics}. If the check is successful, they may move the object to any other location in short range.
Before making a telekinesis check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-7: Telekinesis Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the check.

additionalEffects.name: Silhouette
description: Increase the possible silhouette of the targeted object by one. This may be added multiple times, increasing the silhouette by one each time.

additionalEffects.name: Range
description: Increase the range to which the object can be moved by one range band. This may be added multiple times, increasing the range by one range band each time.

additionalEffects.name: Fine Control
description: The user can perform precise manipulation of objects, allowing them to do anything they could normally do with their hands.

additionalEffects.name: Throw
description: The object is thrown with enough force to inflict damage. The damage is 5 for a silhouette 0 object, or 10 times the silhouette for silhouette 1 or higher. For each silhouette beyond 1, upgrade the difficulty of the check once. This is treated as a ranged combat check.

spell.name: Tech Attack
structured: A tech attack describes the use of the omni-tool to disrupt enemy systems or fire flash-forged projectiles at them.

Unlike biotic attacks, tech attacks are further differentiated into a variety of sub-types that have inherent base abilities. Each of these attack types counts as a different readied power on a character's omni-tool.

{@b Incinerate:} The attack gains the {@quality Burn} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}. The attack also gains the {@quality Sunder} quality against the target's armor.

{@b Cryo Blast:} The attack gains the {@quality Ensnare} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}. The character may spend {@symbols t} to {@rule staggered|stagger} a target for one round.

{@b Overload:} The attack gains the {@quality Phasic} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)} divided by 2 and rounded up. The attack also gains the {@quality Sunder} quality against any electronic equipment.

{@b Neural Shock:} The attack gains the {@quality Disorient} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (LifeSci)}. The character may spend {@symbols t} to {@rule staggered|stagger} a target for one round. This attack can only be used against organic targets.

All tech attacks have a default range of short and the default difficulty of the check is {@difficulty average}. The damage dealt is equal to your character's {@characteristic Intellect}, plus 1 damage per uncanceled {@symbols s}. The attack has no Critical rating, but may inflict a Critical Injury with a {@symbols t}.
Before making a tech attack check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-10: Tech Attack Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the attack.

additionalEffects.name: Blast
description: The attack gains the {@quality Blast} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}.

additionalEffects.name: Close Combat
description: May select a target engaged with the character. If the attack has the {@quality Blast} quality, the character is unaffected by it.

additionalEffects.name: Deadly
description: The attack gains a Critical rating of 2. The attack also gains the {@quality Vicious} quality with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)} when used against synthetic targets or {@skill Knowledge (LifeSci)} when used against organic targets. This effect may not be combined with the Non-Lethal effect.

additionalEffects.name: Impact
description: The attack gains the {@quality Knockdown} quality. If the attack hits, you may spend {@symbols a} to move the target up to one range band horizontally.

additionalEffects.name: Non-Lethal
description: The attack gains the {@quality Stun Damage} quality.

additionalEffects.name: Anti-Synthetic
description: When dealing damage to a synthetic target, each {@symbols s} deals +2 damage instead of +1. This effect can only be applied to Overload.

additionalEffects.name: Anti-Organic
description: When dealing damage to an organic target, each {@symbols s} deals +2 damage instead of +1. This effect can only be applied to Incinerate, Cryo Blast and Neural Shock.

additionalEffects.name: Range
description: Increase the range of the attack by one range band. This may be added multiple times, increasing the range by one range band each time.

additionalEffects.name: Priming
description: The attack deals no damage, but any of its qualities may still be activated if it hits. This effect may not be combined with the Deadly, Blast or Detonating effects.

additionalEffects.name: Multi-Target
description: The attack gains the {@quality Auto-fire} quality. The increased difficulty to use the quality is already included in the difficulty modifier.

additionalEffects.name: Detonating
description: The attack deals damage equal to twice the character's {@characteristic Intellect}. If the attack has the {@quality Blast} quality, it affects all characters within short range instead of engaged.

spell.name: Tech Construct
structured: Using the omni-tool's fabricator and flash-forge systems, a tech specialist can summon a variety of constructs to suit their needs. To do so, the character makes an {@difficulty average|Tech}. If successful, the construct appears at engaged range with the character and persists until the end of the character's next turn, though their presence can be extended by use of the {@rule Concentrate|concentrate maneuver}.
Each of the following sub-types of tech constructs counts as a different readied power on a character's omni-tool.
{@b Barricade:} Constructs an instant barricade to serve as {@rule cover}, which provides a ranged defense of 2 for up to three characters.

{@b Combat Drone:} Summons a {@adversary combat drone} rival NPC. The drone takes its turn immediately after the character. It acts independently but is loyal to its owner. The character may use a maneuver to direct the drone, determining its maneuver and action. The stats for the drone are found on page 113.

{@b Decoy:} Creates a stationary holographic construct, mimicking the character's appearance. While engaged with a character, upgrade the difficulty of all combat checks targeting them once. While the decoy is further away, at the GM's discretion, a foe may choose to attack the decoy out of confusion.

{@b Supply Pylon:} Deploys an immobile pylon that supplies ammunition. Any character engaged with a supply pylon may spend a maneuver to retrieve and immediately use a {@gear spare thermal clip} from the pylon, reloading their weapon if it has run out of ammo.
Before making a tech construct check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-11: Tech Construct Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the check.

additionalEffects.name: Range
description: Increase the range at which the construct is summoned by one range band. This may be added multiple times, increasing the range by one range band each time.

additionalEffects.name: Detonate
description: On their turn, the character may spend a maneuver to detonate a construct summoned with this modifier. The construct is destroyed and any characters engaged with it take damage equal to the character's {@characteristic Intellect} plus their ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}.

spell.name: Sabotage
structured: Sabotage is a general term for any powers that disrupt synthetic targets or the electronic devices of an organic target.
Your character selects one target within short range, then chooses one of the following effects and makes an {@difficulty average|Tech}. If the check is successful, the effect is applied.

{@b Invasion:} Until the end of the character's next turn, the target decreases the ability of any relevant skill checks they make by one (in effect, this means they remove one {@dice ability} from their checks). On a synthetic target, this includes all skill checks, but for an organic target, it depends on the device targeted (for instance their weapon, omni-tool or biotic amp).

{@b Overheat:} The target's weapon immediately runs out of ammunition and may not be used until the end of the encounter. This effect does not benefit from the {@rule Concentrate|concentration maneuver}.

{@b Energy Drain:} Until the end of the character's next turn, the target's ranged and melee defense is decreased by an amount up to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}. The character's ranged and melee defense are increased by the same amount.
{@b Tactical Scan:} Until the end of the character's next turn, all combat checks directed at the target reduce their Critical rating by 1 (to a minimum of 1).

{@b VI Hacking:} The difficulty of the check becomes {@difficulty daunting}. At the GM's discretion, this check can instead be an opposed {@skill Tech} versus {@skill Computers} check. Until the end of the character's next turn, the target obeys the character's commands. The character may spend a maneuver to direct the target, allowing them to determine its action and maneuver. VI Hacking can only be used on synthetic targets such as mechs.

Unlike {@spell Tech Attack|tech attacks} and {@spell Tech Construct|tech constructs}, these different effects do not count as occupying separate slots on the omni-tool and are all available when the sabotage power is readied.
Before making a sabotage check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-12: Sabotage Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the check.

additionalEffects.name: Damping
description: After the target makes a check, you may change one {@dice setback} to a face displaying a {@symbols f}.

additionalEffects.name: Range
description: Increase the range of the power by one range band. This may be added multiple times, increasing the range by one range band each time.

additionalEffects.name: Additional Target
description: The power affects one additional target within range. In addition, after using the power, you may spend {@symbols a} to affect one additional target within range (and may trigger this multiple times, spending {@symbols a} each time).

additionalEffects.name: Malfunction
description: After a target makes a check, you may change any one die in the pool not displaying a {@symbols t} or {@symbols d} to a different face.

spell.name: Tech Augment
structured: Tech abilities can be used to augment a target's abilities, improving their weaponry or defenses or cloaking their presence. Each of the following sub-types of augments counts as a different readied power on a character's omni-tool. To use this power select one target in engaged range (which may be the character themselves) and make an {@difficulty average|Tech}. If successful, the target is affected by the tech augment until the end of the character's next turn.

{@b Tech Armor:} Projects a layer of omni-tech armor around the target. Reduces the damage of all hits they suffer by one, and further reduce it by one for every uncanceled {@symbols ss} beyond the first.

{@b Charged Melee:} The target's {@skill Brawl} and {@skill Melee} weapon attacks gain the {@quality Stun} and {@quality Phasic} qualities, each with a rating equal to the character's ranks in {@skill Knowledge (PhysSci)}.
{@b Turbocharge:} The target may use the {@quality Auto-fire} quality on their {@skill Ranged (Light)} and {@skill Ranged (Heavy)} weapons without increasing the difficulty of their combat checks.

{@b Tactical Cloak:} The target is rendered invisible. All opponents disengage from the target and may not engage them for the duration of the power. The target counts as fully concealed and adds {@dice setback|3} to all combat, {@skill Perception} and {@skill Vigilance} checks targeting them as well as {@dice boost|3} to any {@skill Stealth} checks they make.
Before making an augment check, choose any number of additional effects listed on {@b {@table 3-13: Tech Augment Additional Effects}}. These effects are added to the check.

vehicle.name: Crewed Mech
description: {@i Example Models: Atlas, Triton ADS}
While not as often employed as the automated VI-controlled mechs, these large walkers are powerful combat units that can do tremendous damage to infantry units.

vehicle.name: Exploration Rover
description: {@i Example Models: ND1 Nomad}
Designed for planetside exploration, these quick, wheeled vehicles are outfitted with all-terrain drive, boosters, and partial life-support systems.
Exploration rovers ignore {@dice setback} added to {@skill Driving} checks due to uneven terrain.

vehicle.name: Heavy Infantry Fighting Vehicle
description: {@i Example Models: M29 Grizzly, Krogan Tomkah}

These heavy duty combat vehicles are designed to carry soldiers around combat zones and offer fire-support. Their large size stems from the heavy armor plating they are outfitted with, which renders any personal arms ineffectual, though it leaves them with a rather cramped and uncomfortable interior. Then again, military transports were not designed with comfort in mind.

vehicle.name: Hovertank
description: {@i Example Models: M-44 Hammerhead}

A more unique approach to replacing wheeled and tracked vehicles, hovertanks have the advantage of being able to navigate nearly any terrain with ease. The downside however is their high energy consumption and tendency to overheat, which makes them unsuitable to long-term missions.
Hovertanks ignore {@dice setback|2} added to {@skill Driving} checks due to uneven terrain, can hover over water and across narrow crevices.

vehicle.name: Light Infantry Fighting Vehicle
description: {@i Example Models: M35 Mako}

Smaller, lighter and faster than its heavy variant, the light IFV was designed to allow rapid deployment and transport within the cargo bays of smaller ships such as {@vehicle frigate|frigates}. Its increased maneuverability stems from a refined thruster system and integrated mass effect field generator which also allows the vehicle to be airdropped relatively safely.

vehicle.name: Cargo Shuttle
description: These bulky freight shuttles serve as small distance cargo transports or assist in unloading the very large freight-cruisers that are incapable of atmospheric entry. Their mid-range size allows them to still fit on landing platforms but also makes them compatible with magnetic arm tether systems found more commonly on space stations.

vehicle.name: Dropshuttle
description: {@i Example Models: UT-47 Kodiak, Andromeda SH3}

Dropshuttles are personnel carriers that offer interplanetary transport with limited FTL capabilities. The detriments of their blocky shape and high weight are canceled by a powerful eezo core, allowing the ship to fly despite the laws of physics. Its tough armor, strong barrier generators and life support systems unfortunately leave little space for control assisting systems, making them difficult to handle. Despite this, they are still the most popular deployment method among most any military, mercenary faction or law enforcement community.

vehicle.name: Heavy Freighter
vehicle.complement: 1 pilot, 1 co-pilot, 1 cargo master, up to 20 crew
description: {@i Example Models: Athabasca-class, Ballard-class}

These large transport ships traverse the galaxy carrying masses of cargo between planets. From collecting produce from highly industrialized worlds to supplying new colonies with equipment housing, there are few things that wouldn't fit within the ship.

While its length is similar to that of the smaller freighters, its cargo capacity is increased greatly due to fielding twice the amount of modular containers in a stacked arrangement. Unfortunately this greatly impacts the ship's maneuverability. Freighter captains often make use of shuttles to deliver their cargo planet-side, rather than put these vehicles under the stress of atmospheric entry.

vehicle.name: Light Freighter
description: {@i Example Models: Kowloon-class}

The smaller cousin of the {@vehicle heavy freighter}, these models do not use two levels of cargo containers. This reduces their profile, improves their thrust-to-mass ratio and has them require smaller eezo cores, therefore making them far more popular for short distance transfer. These ships are also under much less stress when operating within atmosphere, allowing them to make planet-side deliveries without auxiliary transports.

vehicle.name: Passenger Liner
description: These interplanetary transport vessels are designed for comfortable travel for people who do not own their own ship. While their outside appearances and internal layout may differ greatly between models, their overall resilience, speed and performance can be represented by this profile.
A passenger liner can increase its passenger capacity to 40 by reducing its encumbrance capacity to 0.

vehicle.name: Luxury Liner
description: For the upper class of space travelers, these luxurious transports provide comfort and amenities - though their ticket prices are much higher. It is not unheard of for corporate executives or high-ranking members of government to privately own these vessels and use them to conduct their business around the galaxy.

vehicle.name: Skycar
description: {@i Example Models: X3M}

The most common vehicle traveling around the Citadel, as well as many other civilized worlds such as Illium, skycars are the most common mode for transportation - either privately owned, or in the form of automated taxis or rentable public transit. They are able to fly up to a few hundred meters above the ground and are outfitted with vacuum seals for short-term operation outside a planet's or station's atmosphere.

vehicle.name: Fighter
description: {@i Example Models: F-61 Trident}

These lightweight, maneuverable vessels are designed for combat against capital ships. Deployed in squadrons from their {@vehicle carrier|carriers}, they are used in risky assault maneuvers, breaking through point defense systems and delivering their lethal payloads.

vehicle.name: Gunship

abilities.name: Variable Loadout
abilities.description: Gunships can be equipped with a diverse set of weapons or hull modifications. The following examples display some of the possible configurations and their additional costs.

children.name: Bomber
children.description: The gunship gains the following weapon, occupying 2 hard points and reducing its passenger capacity to 0: {@b Ventral bomb bay} - can only be used against surface targets (Fire Arc Down; Damage 8; Critical 3; Range [Short]; {@quality Blast|Blast 7}; {@quality Breach|Breach 6}; {@quality Limited Ammo|Limited Ammo 10}). {@b Price/Rarity:} 9,000 credits (R)/6

children.name: Carrier
children.description: The gunship can transport a single silhouette 2 vehicle or mech on a ventral attachment point which occupies 2 hard points. The pilot may deploy the vehicle or mech as an {@rule Incidentals|incidental}. While carrying a vehicle, the gunship's {@rule handling} is reduced by 2. {@b Price/Rarity:} 3,000 credits/4

children.name: Dropship
children.description: The gunship increases its passenger capacity to 10, reduces its hard points by 2 and gains the following weapons: {@b 2 machinegun turrets} (Fire Arc All; Damage 12; Critical 3; Range [Long]; {@quality Auto-fire}, {@quality Personal Scale}, {@quality Pierce|Pierce 3}, {@quality Vicious|Vicious 2}). {@b Price/Rarity:} 8,000 credits/5

description: {@i Example Models: A-61 Mantis}

Gunships are highly configurable weapons platforms designed to be fit into a variety of roles on the battlefield depending on their equipment. Ranging from anti-personnel gunship, over strategic bomber to transport, these vehicles can be adapted to fit the mission in a matter of hours. While these vehicles are capable of operating in space, they possess no FTL capabilities and can not use mass relays.
Gunship weaponry uses personal scale {@rule range bands}.

vehicle.name: Interceptor
description: Optimized for the defense of capital ships against {@vehicle fighter|fighters} and their destructive torpedoes, interceptors are fast, highly maneuverable and outfitted with weaponry that can easily tear apart small vessels.

vehicle.name: Patrol Corvette

weapons.name: 1 starboard and 1 port turret-mounted accelerator cannon

description: A mainstay in the Citadel Defense Fleet and most species militaries and colony fleets, these vessels are mostly used to display presence in colonized systems and act as minor defense forces around small colonies and larger space stations. Carrying a small complement of officers and marines, and outfitted with a surprising amount of firepower for a ship its size, these patrol boats are to show force within colony space against pirates, slavers and foreign militaries.

vehicle.name: Survey Corvette
description: {@i Example Models: Andromeda Tempest (custom built)}

These exploration and survey ships were built en masse in the early years of colonization. Designed to chart new systems, explore beyond unknown relays and find habitable planets, they are outfitted with long-term life-support systems and advanced scanners and probe launch bays.
A survey corvette is outfitted with the {@gear Advanced Sensor Suite|Advanced Sensor Suite (Terrain)} attachment, occupying 1 of its 4 hard points.
{@b Control Skill:} {@skill Operating} or {@skill Piloting}.

vehicle.name: Frigate
description: {@i Example Models: Normandy-class}

Frigates are light escort and scouting vessels designed to function as anti-fighter defense for larger capital ships. Outfitted with large drive cores and thrusters, powerful sensor arrays and light armaments, they function to support the remainder of the fleet with tactical information, dismantle enemy {@vehicle fighter} squadrons and attack unprotected enemy capital ships in small flotillas of four to six. Due to their lower weight and profile, they are the only capital ships capable of landing on planets, even those with high {@rule gravity}.
Frigates are typically outfitted with the {@gear Advanced Sensor Suite|Advanced Sensor Suite (Tactics)} and {@gear GARDIAN Lasers|GARDIAN Laser} attachments, occupying 3 of their 4 hard points.

vehicle.name: Cruiser

abilities.name: Massive 1
abilities.description: When making an attack targeting this vessel, treat the Critical rating of any weapons used as 1 higher.

weapons.name: 4 dorsal and 4 ventral turret-mounted heavy accelerator cannons

description: {@i Example Models: Geneva-class, Hensa-class}

The middle-weight class of capital ships, cruisers form the majority of all galactic navies. With powerful hull, shields and armaments, they are able to cause large amounts of damage in fleet battle and orbital assaults, while still remaining more maneuverable than their {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts}. Beyond their role as the main force in major fleet engagements, they serve as symbols of power in colonized space and remote systems, leading campaigns against pirates and casting an aura of authority and protection.
All cruisers are outfitted with the {@gear GARDIAN Lasers|GARDIAN Laser} attachment, occupying 2 of their 4 hard points.

vehicle.name: Carrier
vehicle.complement: 700 to 1,200 officers, pilots and enlisted crew

abilities.name: Massive 1
abilities.description: When making an attack targeting this vessel, treat the Critical rating of any weapons used as 1 higher.

weapons.name: 4 starboard and 4 port turret-mounted twin heavy accelerator cannons
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Starboard and Aft or Forward, Port and Aft

description: These massive, dreadnought-sized vessels are a recent addition to fleet engagements. Introduced by humanity, transposing the concept of naval warfare into space, these ships are designed to host countless squadrons of {@vehicle fighter|fighters}, bombers and {@vehicle interceptor|interceptors} as their main armament, deploying them to attack enemy capital ships and protect their own fleets against incoming small craft. Carriers stay mostly clear of the battle after deploying their complements, as their flight deck configurations leave them with comparatively little armor compared to other capital ships.
All carriers are outfitted with the {@gear GARDIAN Lasers|GARDIAN Laser} attachment, occupying 2 of their 3 hard points.
